title: OpenMoat policy, schema version 1
description: The person's policy (~/.moat/policy.yaml), docs/POLICY.md §1. Checks the shape only: `openmoat policy lint` also checks patterns, unique rule ids and the rules between keys. Unknown keys are rejected.
$comment: Hand-written; crates/openmoat-core/tests/policy_schema/ keeps it equal to the Rust model (Policy and every section). A key added to the model needs a property here.

not.description: A file with both `ask:` and `review:` is an error.

version.description: The policy schema version (ADR-103); only 1 exists.

scope.description: Reserved: accepted so older files stay valid, no effect yet (`policy lint` says so).

project_roots.description: Reserved; the project root is the git root of the call's working directory.

deny.description: Evaluated first; a match here is final.

review.description: Evaluated third: OpenMoat holds the call for the person to review.

ask.description: The name of `review:` before 0.14.0 (ADR-053): still read, never written. `openmoat policy migrate` renames it.

defer.description: Evaluated fourth: the agent's own permission prompt decides (ADR-025).

approval.description: Reserved: accepted so older files stay valid, no effect yet (`policy lint` says so). Approvals are made with `openmoat allow`.

executables.description: Pin program names to absolute paths (§8.1).

additionalProperties.description: The absolute paths this program may run from.

secrets.description: Values OpenMoat keeps from the agent and `openmoat proxy` puts into one header of requests to one host (§2.1).

requests.description: Method and path rules for allowed hosts (§2.3, ADR-062); they only narrow what `net` and `fetch` allow.

requests_untrusted.description: Your own policy only: what `openmoat proxy` does with a connection to a `requests:` host it cannot terminate. Default `refuse`.

require_signed_repo_policy.description: Trust a repository policy only when signed by a key you trusted (§10). Default false.

unattended.description: Your own policy only: what a `defer` becomes when the agent asks no one (§5.4, ADR-102). Default `defer`; `review` holds it.

anyOf.description: The name of `review` before 0.14.0 (ADR-053): still read, never written.

defaults.description: The verdict when no rule matches: one verdict for everything, or a map per kind with "*" as the fallback. Default `review`.

anyOf.description: Keys other than the ten kinds and "*" are accepted but never consulted.

*.description: Every kind without its own entry.

fetch.description: Unset, a fetch takes the `net` default.

web.search.description: Only `defaults` decide a web search; unset, it takes "*".

tool.unknown.description: Only `defaults` decide a tool the adapter cannot classify; unset, it takes "*".

ruleGroup.description: A named group of patterns (§2); it matches when any pattern matches an atomic action of its kind. `policy lint` needs at least one pattern and ids unique across the lists.

id.description: Stable id; shown to the agent and stored in the audit log.

title.description: One line, at most 80 characters: heads the block message (ADR-059).

why.description: One line, at most 160 characters: why the rule exists.

net.description: Host globs for any network access, fetches included.

fetch.description: Host globs for a host's own fetch tool only.

hook_only.description: `deny` groups with `fs.read` or `fs.write` only: the hook applies it, the OS layers leave its paths to the other rules (ADR-034).

sandbox.description: What the operating-system layers need beyond the rules (§9, ADR-018). Your own policy only.

read_roots.description: Paths the OS layers let commands read although no allow rule covers them; absolute or `~/…`, never a glob.

proxy_port.description: Opt-in: the loopback port `openmoat proxy` listens on for host sandbox traffic.

proxy_allow_ech.description: Let `openmoat proxy` forward encrypted server names (ECH). Default false.

proxy_serve_without_credential.description: Let `openmoat proxy` serve requests with no session credential (ADR-044). Default false.

package_min_release_age_days.description: `openmoat run` keeps npm and uv off versions newer than this many days (§9.1); 0 is off. Default 7.

env.description: What `openmoat run` passes on of the environment it starts from (§9.6, ADR-105): `scrubbed` passes only its allowlist, `inherited` everything. Default `inherited`; `require.run: full-boundary` scrubs whatever this says.

env_allow.description: Variables `openmoat run` passes on when it scrubs the environment (§9.3, §9.6); names only, never a pattern.

project_top.description: What `openmoat run` without bubblewrap on Linux grants at the project's top (§9.4). Default `protected`.

project_hook_off.description: What `openmoat run` does when a project's file would turn the agent's hook off (§9.5). Default `refuse`.

id.description: Lowercase letters, digits and `-`; unique. Names the placeholder.

host.description: One host, exact: a lowercase DNS name or IPv4 literal, no pattern or port.

header.description: The request header the value goes in.

plain_http.description: Also inject into plain-HTTP (clear-text) requests. Default false.

port.description: With `plain_http` only: the port those requests go to. Default 80.

tls.description: `terminate`: inside `openmoat run`, decrypt HTTPS to the host and inject there (ADR-043).

allow.description: With `tls` or `plain_http`: the only requests that get the value, `METHOD /path` each.

secretSource.description: Where OpenMoat reads the value: exactly one of `file`, `env`, `keychain`, `command`.

env.description: An environment variable of the `openmoat proxy` process.

keychain.description: An item in the operating system's keychain.

commandSource.description: A program `openmoat proxy` runs for a short-lived value (§2.2, ADR-087; preview).

run.description: The program, absolute or under `~/`, then its arguments; run without a shell.

lifetime.description: The longest one value is used: `90s`, `15m` or `1h`, from 1m to 12h.

refresh_before.description: How long before expiry a new value is asked for; a fifth of `lifetime` when unset (at least 10s).

home.description: The program's `HOME`: an empty folder of its own (`private`, the default) or yours (`user`).

host.description: One lowercase DNS name: no address, port or pattern.

allow.description: Your own policy only: requests that may be sent, `METHOD /path` each; empty, every request `deny` does not name.

deny.description: Requests that are refused, whatever `allow` or a secret's rules say.

hook_only.description: The hook holds the rules, the proxy does not. Default false.

taint.description: What session taint protects beyond the built-in list (§4.1).

protected_writes.description: Path globs whose writes need review once the session read untrusted content; no `!`.

metadata_tools.description: More MCP tools, by full name, whose results are metadata, not content (ADR-057).

defined_servers.description: MCP servers a configuration defines; the built-in metadata tools never belong to one.

provenance.description: Taint follows written files (§4.1.1, ADR-029). Default true.

staging.description: Since 0.17.0: when a session counts as collecting outside the project (§4.5, ADR-061).

outside_reads.description: Distinct files read outside the project; default 25, 0 turns this trigger off.

outside_folders.description: Distinct folders read outside the project; default 2, 0 turns this trigger off.

ignore.description: Path globs whose reads never count, beside the built-in caches; no `!`.

mcp.description: How `openmoat mcp proxy` treats servers and tools (§8).

trust_first_sight.description: Pin a new server's first tool listing unseen (ADR-032). Default false.

browser_open.description: A browser MCP page open is a `fetch` (the default) or a `net` connection (ADR-047).

flow_trusted.description: Since 0.16.0: servers whose results may reach other servers' acting tools unreviewed (ADR-058).

checkDiff.description: Since 0.16.0: levels of `openmoat policy check-diff`'s content checks (ADR-055, MERGE_CHECK.md).

require.description: The least protection level of each agent; below it every call is denied (§9.2, ADR-064). A repository policy or pack can only raise it.

run.description: `openmoat run` starts only with its full boundary (§9.3, ADR-077).

agents.description: Per agent, by host id (as `openmoat status` names it), in place of `protection` for it.
